**What I expect a good study to propose, from this blind pass alone (written before reading it):** (i) time stamps from the clock, by a script rather than a text rule (B3); (ii) a STATUS file shape with a short head and an archive (B4); (iii) a "tool before grind" line in briefs, if the record shows a grind (B2); (iv) a register of reusable programs, if duplication is on the record (B15); (v) possibly one lint class for qualitative-agreement wording (B9); (vi) an outside human reader for what the program publishes, as a practice rather than a binding rule (B11, B14). And it must report the post's "footgun" remark about Millennium Prize problems (B1) and its evidence that a text rule on time failed (B3).
